title: Unable to add new device using GitHub auth
body:
### What is the issue?

- I signed up using GitHub long time ago
- I currently have active (connected) devices in Tailscale, in personal GitHub tailnet
- Add a new device (tried macOS and Linux, both 1.78.1), login from new device, which opens browser for auth
- Sign in with GitHub, then click "Authorize Tailscale" button
- After redirection it says "Error 500 unable to list GitHub orgs"

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0790c15-e916-4cb4-b06f-a49aae024d99)

Request ID is `REQ-202501210201435d2ea10d3c7182b0`. This issue was also reported as `TSS-51837`. I think it's a backend issue, or something with my account. Searched through Google and GitHub issues and found no such error string.

I don't understand, Tailscale does not need to list my GitHub orgs, I'm adding new device to my personal tailnet. Also I have already granted permissions to some of my GitHub orgs.

### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

_No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
What I've tried:

- Refresh the error page: does not work.
- Revoke Tailscale from GitHub applications settings, and redo "Sign in with GitHub": does not work.
- Try another platform / OS: Tried both macOS and Manajaro Linux, same issue.
- Grant one more GitHub org permisson when authorizing Tailscale: same issue.

> It's too bad that we couldn't add other login methods alongside GitHub for situations like this

Tailscale does not handle authentication, so multiple different auth providers would result in multiple different tailnets. That's reasonable for me.

It's just very confusing that they did not mention the auth key on the "add device" UI. I only heard it today.

comments.author: participant20
comments.body:
> Is there any workaround for SSH login?

You should be able to login using SSH. My problem was that I had enabled "check" on my SSH connections in the ACL, which of course fails due to the issue. I changed my ACL to "accept" and I am able to login.

> > Is there any workaround for SSH login?

> You should be able to login using SSH. My problem was that I had enabled "check" on my SSH connections in the ACL, which of course fails due to the issue. I changed my ACL to "accept" and I am able to login.

This was really helpful. I guess for anyone who isn't in an organization that requires strict checks when logging in (in which case you shouldn't be using github auth), setting the ACLs to "accept" should be ... acceptable.
